design.colorMode: light-first public website with dark application shell

must: Pair status colour with text and marker
avoid: Raw colour values in feature components

decisions: Blue actions, cyan live states, teal provisional positive states, emerald settled success
Geist and Geist Mono with tabular numeric treatment
CSS custom properties are the theme source of truth
Minimum server-renderable primitives only in Phase 2A
Phase 2B uses Radix for complex accessible interaction with minimal client boundaries
The design-system route remains the primary foundation showcase; Storybook is deferred
Phase 2C uses an expanded desktop sidebar, collapsed tablet sidebar, labelled mobile bottom navigation, and full Sheet drawer from one typed route registry
Phase 2D separates a spacious public header-and-footer shell from the dense authenticated shell and uses restrained token-driven marketing primitives
Phase 2E uses asymmetric editorial analytics, labelled demonstrations, varied registers instead of repetitive cards, and loss-first transparency
The homepage redesign uses a matchroom dossier direction: oversized editorial type, an instrument-panel research stage, chapter numbering, evidence rails, and loss-first settlement storytelling

The public website uses a Sportradar-referenced sports-technology direction: white and midnight navy foundation, hot red-orange action colour, oversized uppercase statements, hard editorial divisions, and full-width spatial rhythm while preserving original PlayToday content and routes
The refined homepage keeps the public colour system but uses moderate display sizes, a quieter split hero, fewer visible grid lines, product-first sequencing, and one dominant idea per section

The final homepage rebuild uses original matchday editorial photography, narrative feature scenes, a physical settlement receipt, and restrained evidence UI; it removes the prior dashboard-led homepage composition entirely
Homepage controls use a shared 44px-plus touch model, full-width mobile CTA groups, balanced wrapping, and staged 56rem/44rem/24rem responsive refinements for intermediate and small screens

The post-hero homepage uses a light editorial-product system: off-white atmosphere, floating white instruments, paper-like records, rounded analytical surfaces, and red/navy only as restrained accents rather than large grid backgrounds
evidence: Carbon, Primer, and Atlassian data-visualisation accessibility guidance
